extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy (metaphysics); scholars of Schopenhauer
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and explicating Schopenhauer's standards and conceptual criteria about knowledge, the thing-in-itself, and the will as presented in The World as Will and Representation. Focuses on how phenomena, causality, and individuality relate to the will.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time, space, and causality as forms of intuition (phenomenal forms)
rubrics_metrics.description: "We have learnt from the great Kant that time, space, and causality, with their entire constitution, and the possibility of all their forms, are present in our consciousness quite independently of the objects which appear in them... we may call them either forms of intuition or perception of the subject, or qualities of the object as object..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These forms are a priori aspects of knowledge (forms of the principle of sufficient reason) and belong only to phenomena/ideas, not to the thing-in-itself; they are the irreducible boundary between subject and object and condition how objects appear in perception.

rubrics_metrics.name: A priori forms afford exhaustive (but formal) knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: "Only that which depends entirely upon being an object of knowledge... which therefore belongs without distinction to everything that is known... can afford us without reserve a sufficient, exhaustive knowledge... This consists of nothing but those forms of all phenomena of which we are conscious a priori..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mathematics and pure natural science, grounded in a priori forms (time, space, causality), give the clearest and most exhaustive knowledge of form (relations, quantity, position) but supply only form without full content about the inner nature (thing-in-itself).

rubrics_metrics.name: Thing-in-itself identified as will
rubrics_metrics.description: "Are these ideas... something more than or apart from the fact that they are ideas...? The thing-in-itself? The will, we have answered... The name will denotes that which is the inner nature of everything in the world, and the one kernel of every phenomenon."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schopenhauer takes the thing-in-itself to be will: an inner, groundless reality that underlies phenomena and is not itself a form of representation; subsequent claims about forces, character, and individuation flow from this identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Forces of nature as immediate manifestations/objectifications of will (qualitates occultae)
rubrics_metrics.description: "They are in themselves immediate manifestations of will, just as much as human action; and as such they are groundless, like human character... the forces themselves remain qualitates occultae."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forces such as gravity, magnetism, electricity, chemical affinities, etc., are expressions of will. Their particular manifestations obey causality in time/space, but their inner nature is inexplicable and cannot be deduced etiologically; they are prior presuppositions rather than effects or causes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original forces are not causes/effects but prior presupposed conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: "They themselves, on the other hand, can never be called either effect or cause, but are the prior and presupposed conditions of all causes and effects through which their real nature unfolds and reveals itself... It is therefore senseless to demand a cause of gravity or electricity..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When explaining particular manifestations we refer to causes within time/space, but we must not treat the original force as produced by or identical with any cause; it lies outside the chain of causes and effects (outside the principle of sufficient reason).

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplicity and individuation are phenomenal; the thing-in-itself is indivisible
rubrics_metrics.description: "We know that multiplicity in general is necessarily conditioned by space and time... the thing-in-itself... regarded as such and apart from its manifestation, it lies outside time and space, and therefore knows no multiplicity, and is consequently one."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiplicity (parts, number, difference) applies only to appearances (objectifications of will) in time and space; the will itself is undivided and is present whole in every manifestation, so numerical increase of phenomena does not imply division of the thing-in-itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grades of objectification correspond to Platonic Ideas
rubrics_metrics.description: "These different grades of the objectification of will... as their unattained types or as the eternal forms of things... are, I say, simply Plato's Ideas. By Idea, then, I understand every definite and fixed grade of the objectification of will..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schopenhauer equates Plato's Ideas with fixed grades of the will's objectification (eternal forms/prototypes). Use 'Idea' in this Platonic sense — not as Kantian abstract concepts — when discussing types or grades of manifestation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Higher grades show stronger individuality; lower grades lose individuality
rubrics_metrics.description: "In the higher grades of the objectivity of will we see individuality occupy a prominent position, especially in the case of man... The farther down we go, the more completely is every trace of the individual character lost in the common character of the species... Finally, in the inorganic kingdom of nature all individuality disappears."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of organisms/objects should account for degree of objectification: plants show less individual character than animals, animals less than humans, and inorganic bodies display almost no individuality (crystals excepted). Corollaries include physiological correlates (brain convolutions) and behavioral differences (sexual choice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological priority: start from self-knowledge to infer other inner natures
rubrics_metrics.description: "We ... start from that which is immediately and most completely known to us... my body is the only object of which I know not merely the one side... but also the other side which is called will. Thus... I must, seeing that I seek philosophy and not etiology, learn to understand from my own movements following upon motives the inner nature of the simplest... movements of an unorganised body..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophical inquiry into the thing-in-itself should begin with immediate self-experience (our own will/character) and project that inner knowledge by analogy onto other phenomena, rather than attempting to reduce inner life to mechanistic etiology.

rubrics_metrics.name: The relation between necessity and reality in knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: "Therefore the more necessity any knowledge carries with it... the clearer and more sufficing then it is, the less pure objective content it has, or the less reality, properly so called, is given in it. And conversely, the more there is in it which must be conceived as mere chance... the more proper objectivity and true reality is there in such knowledge..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Knowledge that exhibits strong a priori necessity (e.g., geometric/mathematical knowledge) is formally clear but contains less 'reality' about the thing-in-itself; empirical, contingent knowledge (with elements of chance) reveals more of true reality and the inexplicable content of phenomena.

rubrics_metrics.name: Etiological reduction is limited and cannot reach inner nature
rubrics_metrics.description: "Mechanics, physics, and chemistry teach the rules and laws according to which the forces... operate; that is to say, the law, the rule which these forces observe whenever they enter time and space. But do what we will, the forces themselves remain qualitates occultae... the thing-in-itself can never be completely fathomed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scientific/etiological accounts explain how manifestations occur in time/space but cannot exhaustively explain the inner being (the will) that underlies these manifestations; attempts to reduce life and mind wholly to physico-chemical mechanisms leave an inexplicable residuum.
